label: AGENT-SIMULATED PERSONA RUNS. One AI agent played every persona. These are not real learners, not human results, and not the cross-model blind design originally planned.
performed_by: One AI agent (Kiro workflow agent, single model) inside the build environment. No API calls, no second model, no human.
scenario_source: src/scenario.twee at commit 6101ae0 (option order as published: D1 A=strong, B=avoidant, C=mistake; D2 A=avoidant, B=strong, C=mistake; D3 A=avoidant, B=mistake, C=strong)
known_bias: The agent read the full scenario source (including outcome passages, the debrief that names strong/mistake/avoidant, and the earlier agent review's flag prediction) before playing. Choices are its judgment of how each persona would realistically act, not a blind reaction.
scoring: strong +1, mistake 0, avoidant -1; score >= 3 Improved, 0 to 2 Unresolved, < 0 Escalated (same logic as the scenario)

decisions.reason: I'm not ready to make this a thing in front of Marcus. I'll check how she is first and see if she brings it up.
She has been here nine years and she's upset. I've already made her feel attacked; I'd rather drop it than lose her.
She's exhausted and proud of the flu cover. I want her to leave feeling good, so I'd wrap the handover point in praise.

reflection.clarity: None of the options felt obviously right in the moment. In Decision 2 the long option sounded like what a confident manager says, which is exactly what I don't feel like.
reflection.realism: Very real. Being promoted over former peers and avoiding the conversation is what I'd do.

decisions.reason: The job aid says name the specific moment and ask 'What's your take?'. That line is basically on my sheet, so I'd use it even though I'm nervous.

reflection.clarity: Decisions 1 and 2 felt easy only because the job aid gives me those exact sentences. Decision 3 was genuinely hard.
reflection.realism: Realistic. The tired, proud colleague in Decision 3 is the situation where I'd slip.

reflection.realism: Realistic. The clinic runs on throughput and the one-on-one is the first thing I'd drop.
